etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French genereux, and its source, Latin generōsus (“of noble birth”), from genus (“race, stock”).

definitions.definition: Noble in behaviour or actions; principled, not petty; kind, magnanimous. [from 16th c.]
Willing to give and share unsparingly; showing a readiness to give more (especially money) than is expected or needed. [from 17th c.]
Large, more than ample, copious. [from 17th c.]

quote.citation: 1932, Delos W. Lovelace, King Kong, published 1965, page 4:
quote.text: [H]is hard jaw worked slowly upon a generous mouthful of plug cut.

quote.citation: 2018, Tayari Jones, An American Marriage, Oneworld Publications, page 226:
quote.text: The ice cream parlors served generous scoops, hand-dipped by college-bound teenagers who spoke through colorful orthodontia.
